 COLUMBIA — A reserve South Carolina football player is no longer with the team after getting in trouble with the law.
 Kicker Upton Bellenfant was listed as an inmate in the York County Detention Center as of 8:20 p.m. on Wednesday, according to online judicial records. He was booked into jail at 6:12 a.m. on Wednesday on a charge of driving under the influence. 
 By 8:32 p.m., he was no longer listed as a current inmate. His bond was $1,224.
 His specific charge was first offense with a blood alcohol level of greater than .10 percent but less than .16 percent. The state limit is .08. He was arrested by the S.C. State Highway Patrol.
 "We are aware of the situation. Upton is no longer a member of our football program," read a statement from a school spokesperson. "We have no further comment at this time."
 Bellenfant has not played this season. He transferred from Texas Tech and was competing for the starting place-kicker job with Max Kelley and Malik Orsan, who won the job.
